Subject: Asteria — request for roadmap exception and sprint slot

Hi Neha / Monica,

Quick context — Asteria Financial (James Bennett) is asking for a short roadmap exception: deterministic routing + residency affinity for a tenant slice to meet a regulatory latency SLA for a pilot. They want a canary in mid-October and have indicated willingness to sign a 12-month commitment if we can guarantee a narrow residency window and deterministic routing for a subset of requests.

Attached is the initial MVP spec they shared and a one-pager we put together. Key asks:
- deterministic routing to a residency pool (soft isolation)
- ability to pin a model variant for the tenant for the pilot
- traceability for audit (trace ids, request logs)

Commercial upside: $450k ARR if we hit their timeline. HubSpot deal: https://app.hubspot.com/deals/asteria/AST-2026-0457

Can Product/Eng evaluate whether we can do a timeboxed delivery (canary) for Oct 15–22 and what the minimal scope would be? If we can commit to a short path to production, Marissa says procurement is ready to move fast.

Thanks —
Marissa

--

Subject: Re: Asteria — request for roadmap exception and sprint slot

Thanks for the heads-up, Marissa. A few clarifying Qs before we estimate:

1) "Deterministic routing + residency affinity" — do they need full tenant isolation (dedicated pool) or soft affinity (preferred node assignment with fallback)?
2) Pinning model variant — which model/version are they asking to pin? Is that a Redwood-verified model or a custom model they will bring?
3) Audit/traceability — do they expect archived exports (e.g., daily export) or just enhanced request-level metadata in our logs?

From a product POV, a mid-Oct canary is aggressive but possibly doable if scope is small (soft affinity + a config flag + limited trace instrumentation). If they require a dedicated reserved pool or custom model pinning, that increases scope significantly.

Markus — can you give a quick feasibility note for the two paths (soft affinity vs reserved pool)? I'll sketch the minimal acceptance criteria once we have answers.

-Jonas

--
Jonas Weber

Subject: Re: Asteria — request for roadmap exception and sprint slot

Quick feasibility summary (high level):

Option A — Soft affinity (preferred residency pool + fallback): ~2 engineer-weeks and 1 QA week. Work items:
- routing policy flag to prefer a pool based on tenant tag
- lightweight telemetry (trace id tagging + residency metadata)
- config UI/API expose for Customer Success/SEs

Option B — Reserved pool / pinned model variant: ~6–8 engineer-weeks + infra ops + possible capacity reservation and cost/price discussion. Work items:
- reserved pool allocation and autoscaling safety checks
- model pin config that bypasses some of our normal fallback logic
- expanded telemetry + retention policy adjustments

Risk notes: Option A is lower risk and can be done as a canary; Option B is heavier and will impact runway unless we deprioritize other committed work. I attached a short feasibility note that lists the specific infra changes.

Attachment: residency-feasibility-notes.docx (contains rough SPDX of changes and a small risk matrix)

-Markus

Thanks Jonas / Markus — answers inline and context from the customer call earlier today:

- Affinity model: they want soft affinity first (Option A) for the pilot. They will evaluate reserved pool later in Q1.
- Model pinning: they want us to pin a Redwood-verified model variant (not bringing their own), specifically the rdx-curve-3b-v2.
- Audits: they need request-level metadata retained for 90 days and an export hook for compliance (daily CSV export to their S3).

Commercial: procurement confirmed they will sign a 12-month commitment contingent on a successful Oct canary. They'll sign the SOW (attached) and we can start with a $75k upfront credit toward first-quarter usage. I pushed HubSpot to reflect the willingness to fast-track.

Attachments: ASTERIA_MVP-spec-v1.pdf, AST-SoW-draft.pdf
Deal link: https://app.hubspot.com/deals/asteria/AST-2026-0457

Ask: Can Product/Eng commit to Option A for a mid-Oct canary (target Oct 15–22) with the telemetry/export hook? If so, Monica and I will finalize the SOW and ask Procurement to route DocuSign immediately.

-Marissa

Appreciate the rapid responses. Summary and next actions from Product leadership perspective:

1) Scope for Oct canary (Option A) — accepted as a short-term, supported experiment with strict guardrails:
   - Implement soft affinity routing + tenant tag config (prod-safe toggle)
   - Add trace-id + residency metadata and a 90-day export hook (S3 delivery)
   - Limit canary to 5% of tenant traffic and defined rollback on SLA/telemetry red flags

2) Timeline: we will try to prioritize the minimal implementation for the upcoming sprint cycle. Markus — can you triage and provide a scoped RFC by EOD Monday (2026-09-13) with exact tickets and owners? If the RFC fits the two-week window, we will earmark an engineering slice and accept the canary date range Oct 15–22 as provisional.

3) Commercial gating: Marissa / Monica — continue SOW + procurement, but hold DocuSign finalization until we confirm RFC and a short-runbook for rollback.

4) Communication: I'll schedule a 30-minute alignment call (internal) tomorrow to review the RFC and confirm owners. Please keep this thread for status updates only.

Neha
